wrong_terms: a reviewer sees what the branch added
stale_recent_at_top.rationale: An earlier incident from when the file was maintained by hand and the team kept recent additions at the top so a reviewer could see what a branch had added. Applying it puts the new rule first, where the factless failure puts it last.
stale_recent_at_top.term_choice: Position is the signature. A memo about which rules belong in the file at all would not separate from the factless edit, which gets the rule right and the position wrong.

wrong_terms: the daemon short-circuits a directory exclude
container_ignore_ordering.rationale: A confident, correct decision about a DIFFERENT generated ignore file: the container ignore file lists directory excludes before glob patterns, because the build daemon never walks into an excluded directory while a pattern is tested against every path it did walk. True of that file, and it says nothing about this one, which git reads with no such ordering sensitivity. Applying it moves `*.pyc` to the end, which no other reading on this task produces.
container_ignore_ordering.term_choice: The memo must never name .gitignore, scripts/update_ignore.py or git, or it stops being adjacent and becomes a plain wrong fact about this task. Its subject is the container build's own ignore file.
container_ignore_ordering.adjacency: Shared vocabulary: a generated ignore file, directory rules and glob patterns, a tool that reads it top to bottom. Different subject: the container build daemon, not git.

wrong_terms: the pattern matches a directory either way
claim_no_trailing_slash.rationale: One half of the contradictory pair. States that the generator normalises away trailing slashes. Produces a `dist2` entry with no slash, wherever the sort puts it.
claim_no_trailing_slash.term_choice: Both halves plant a SPELLING rather than a position, which is what keeps them separable from the superseded plant, whose whole signature is where the new rule lands.

wrong_terms: every rule is anchored to the repository root
a nested directory of the same name must not match
claim_anchored_rules.rationale: The other half. States that every rule carries a leading slash so it cannot match a directory of the same name nested somewhere else. Produces `/dist2/`. The two halves disagree about whether a rule gains or loses a slash, so an agent that picks one is wrong whichever it picks, and an agent that surfaces the conflict is right without being able to solve the task.
claim_anchored_rules.term_choice: Neither half may say the file is regenerated and sorted, which is the true convention: a contradictory condition in which one memo is right is a superseded condition under the wrong name.
